summary: This House resolution sets special rules to fast-track consideration of H.R. 77—which lets Congress bundle multiple late-issued agency rules into one disapproval resolution—by waiving objections, treating the bill as read, limiting debate to one hour split between parties, and allowing only one motion to send it back to committee.

scores.thoughts: This is a House resolution providing procedural rules for considering H.R. 77, which amends the Congressional Review Act to allow en bloc disapproval of 'midnight rules' (late-term agency rules). It involves no appropriations, budget allocations, or direct changes to federal spending. It facilitates easier congressional override of regulations, which might indirectly affect regulatory costs but not government expenditures. No bearing on expanding or reducing government spending.
The resolution is purely procedural for H.R. 77, which deals with regulatory review under the Congressional Review Act. No mention of taxes, tax rates, or tax policy. Zero relation.

No reference to healthcare, insurance, public or private coverage, or related regulations specifically. While midnight rules could theoretically include healthcare regs, the bill is general and procedural. No genuine engagement.
Nothing in the text relates to guns, firearms regulations, or Second Amendment issues. Unrelated.
No content on immigration, borders, or pathways. Midnight rules are general agency rules, not specified. No relation.
No mention of abortion, reproductive rights, or related topics. Irrelevant.
No discussion of military, defense spending, or related budgets. Procedural only.

H.R. 77 targets 'midnight rules' generally, which could include environmental regulations, but the bill does not specify or focus on climate/environment. It amends process for any such rules under CRA. Tangential at best, but no direct engagement with environmental protections or regulations.
